title: Global Exception Handling with @ControllerAdvice
description: Centralize error handling across all controllers with @ControllerAdvice.

slides.title: One Place to Rule Them All 🏰
slides.content:
# @ControllerAdvice

A class annotated with `@ControllerAdvice` can contain `@ExceptionHandler`, `@InitBinder`, and `@ModelAttribute` methods that apply globally to all controllers.

**Benefits:**
- Centralized error handling.
- Consistent error responses across the entire API.
- No duplication of exception handling code.

quizData.question: Which annotation is used to create a global exception handler class?
quizData.explanation: @ControllerAdvice (or its REST‑specific variant @RestControllerAdvice) is used for global exception handling.

slides.title: Creating a Global Handler
slides.content: Create a class and annotate it with `@RestControllerAdvice` (which combines `@ControllerAdvice` and `@ResponseBody`).

slides.title: Order Matters 📜
slides.content:
# How Exceptions Are Matched

Spring picks the most specific exception handler. For example, if you have handlers for `ResourceNotFoundException` and `Exception`, the former will be used for that specific exception. The generic `Exception` handler acts as a fallback.

**Best Practice:** Always include a generic `Exception` handler to catch any unhandled exceptions and return a friendly error message (without exposing stack traces).

slides.title: Logging Errors 📝
slides.content: Don't forget to log the exception! In your global handler, use a logger to record the error for debugging, while returning a sanitized message to the client.
